title: Living with a Changing Climate
story: Dr. Nadia Rahman is a Bangladeshi climate scientist. She splits her time between a research center in Dhaka and a university in London, where she works with her colleague Tom Baker. Together they study floods, heatwaves and cyclones, and how a changing climate affects daily life and work.
storyBn: ড. নাদিয়া রহমান একজন বাংলাদেশি জলবায়ু বিজ্ঞানী। তিনি ঢাকার একটি গবেষণা কেন্দ্র আর লন্ডনের একটি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে ভাগ করে কাজ করেন; লন্ডনে তার সহকর্মী টম বেকার। তারা একসাথে বন্যা, তাপপ্রবাহ ও ঘূর্ণিঝড় নিয়ে গবেষণা করেন, আর দেখেন বদলে যাওয়া জলবায়ু কীভাবে মানুষের দৈনন্দিন জীবন ও কাজে প্রভাব ফেলছে।

units.focus: Describe changes that are still going on

sessions.pattern: Subject + has/have been + verb-ing + for / since ...
sessions.tipBn: অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনো চলছে এমন কাজ বোঝাতে has/have been + verb-ing বসে, সাথে for বা since থাকে।

items.en: Average temperatures in Bangladesh have been rising steadily for more than four decades.
Nadia has been studying river floods in the northern districts for almost twelve years.
Sea water has been creeping further inland along the southwest coast, ruining farmland.
Garment workers in Gazipur have been struggling with extreme heat inside the factories all summer.
Tom has been collecting rainfall data from local weather stations since the project began.
Monsoon rains have been arriving later and ending more abruptly over the past decade.

sessions.tipBn: has/have এর পরে not been + verb-ing বসিয়ে না-বোধক বাক্য হয়।

items.en: The embankment hasn't been holding up well against the stronger floods of recent years.
In early spring, it hasn't been raining nearly as much as it used to.
Nadia hasn't been sleeping well since the flood warnings started coming in.
Many delivery riders haven't been earning enough because of the relentless rain this month.
Local farmers haven't been planting their usual rice varieties since the soil became salty.
The weather models haven't been performing as reliably as the team expected.

sessions.tipBn: Has/Have শুরুতে বসে, তারপর subject, been এবং verb-ing।

items.en: Have coastal families been moving to Dhaka because of rising sea levels?
Has the research team been tracking changes in the Jamuna's flow since 2015?
Has Tom been working on the heatwave report with the London team all weekend?
Have the forecasts been getting more accurate over the years as satellite technology improves?
Has the river been rising steadily in Sunamganj since the heavy rain began upstream?
Have outdoor workers been taking longer breaks during the hottest hours of the day?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + has/have + subject + been + verb-ing ...?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে has/have, তারপর subject, been এবং verb-ing বসে।

items.en: How long have you been monitoring the water level at this station?
Why have so many farmers in Khulna been switching to salt-tolerant crops?
What has Nadia been telling policymakers about the rising risk of floods?
Where have the displaced families been living since the river swallowed their village?
How have rising temperatures been affecting the health of construction workers in Dhaka?
Which parts of the country have been experiencing longer and more severe dry spells?

sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে has/have been + verb-ing দিয়ে এমন পরিবর্তন বলা হয়েছে যা অনেক দিন ধরে চলছে এবং এখনো থামেনি।

items.title: A hotter Dhaka
items.en: Nadia has been measuring street temperatures in Dhaka for three summers. The city has been growing rapidly, and green spaces have been disappearing to make room for new buildings. As a result, concrete and asphalt have been trapping heat long after sunset. Residents have been complaining that nights no longer offer any relief. Nadia has been sharing her findings with city planners, hoping they will act soon.

items.title: Waiting for the water to fall
items.en: For almost two weeks, the Teesta has been flowing above the danger level. Families in Lalmonirhat have been living on the embankment with their cattle and a few belongings. Aid workers have been delivering rice, clean water and medicine by boat. Children haven't been going to school since the flood began. Everyone has been watching the sky and praying for the rain to stop.

items.title: The view from London
items.en: Tom has been following the weather in Bangladesh closely since he first visited Dhaka in 2019. Back in London, he has been noticing changes too. Summers have been getting hotter, and the city has been dealing with heatwaves it was never designed for. Tom and Nadia have been comparing notes on how two very different cities have been adapting.

units.focus: Explain what had happened before a disaster
units.focusBn: দুর্যোগের আগেই কী ঘটে গিয়েছিল তা ব্যাখ্যা করা

sessions.pattern: Subject + had + past participle ... before / by the time + past simple.
sessions.tipBn: অতীতের দুটি ঘটনার মধ্যে যেটি আগে ঘটেছিল সেটি বোঝাতে had + past participle ব্যবহার হয়।

items.en: By the time the warning reached the village, the river had already burst its banks.
Nadia had studied the area for years before the flood destroyed the old embankment.
The farmers had harvested most of their rice just before the flash flood hit.
After it had rained for five days straight, the roads to Sunamganj became impassable.
Tom had read about monsoon humidity, but he was still shocked when he landed in Dhaka.
The weather office had issued a red alert two days before the cyclone made landfall.

sessions.pattern: Subject + had not (hadn't / had never) + past participle ...
sessions.tipBn: had এর পরে not বা never বসিয়ে পুরাঘটিত অতীতের না-বোধক বাক্য হয়।

items.en: Many villagers hadn't received the warning because the mobile network had gone down.
Tom had never seen a river as wide as the Jamuna before his first visit.
The local authorities hadn't repaired the embankment since the previous flood in 2022.
Even Nadia, with all her experience, hadn't expected the water to rise so quickly overnight.
The families hadn't stored enough dry food before the roads were cut off.
It had not rained that heavily in the region for more than half a century.

sessions.tipBn: অবাক হয়ে বা কোনো কিছু নিশ্চিত হতে Hadn't দিয়ে প্রশ্ন শুরু হয়।

items.en: Hadn't the weather office warned everyone about the storm two days earlier?
Hadn't the villagers moved their cattle to higher ground before the water arrived?
Hadn't Tom packed a raincoat before he left for the field trip?
Hadn't the government promised to strengthen the embankment after the last flood?
Hadn't the river already risen above the danger level by Sunday morning?
Hadn't Nadia told you about the heat before you booked your trip to Rajshahi?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + had + subject + past participle ...?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে had, তারপর subject এবং past participle বসে।

items.en: What had the villagers done to protect their homes before the flood arrived?
How much rain had fallen in the hills before the flash flood reached the town?
Where had the families taken shelter by the time the rescue boats arrived?
Which warning signs had the fishermen noticed before the sea turned rough?
When had Nadia first predicted that this part of the district would flood regularly?
How many homes had the floodwater washed away by the end of the monsoon?

sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে had + past participle দিয়ে বোঝানো হয়েছে কোন ঘটনা আগেই ঘটে গিয়েছিল।

items.title: Too late for the harvest
items.en: By the time the flash flood reached Sunamganj, the hills upstream had received record rainfall. Most farmers had not finished harvesting their rice. Some had tried to cut the crop early, but the water had risen too fast. By evening, months of work had disappeared under the muddy water. Nadia later said that the early warning had come far too late.

items.title: Tom's first monsoon
items.en: Before Tom came to Bangladesh, he had only seen the monsoon on television. He had packed light clothes and a small umbrella, thinking that would be enough. Within an hour of landing, the umbrella had broken in the wind. By the end of his first week, he had bought rubber sandals and a proper raincoat. He later joked that nobody had warned him about the mud.

items.title: The night of the cyclone
items.en: The fishermen of Kutubdia had heard the warning on the radio, but many had decided to stay with their boats. By midnight, the wind had grown so strong that the sea had swept over the embankment. Those who had already moved to the cyclone shelter were safe. Others had to climb onto rooftops and wait for dawn. Afterward, the village leader said the shelter had saved hundreds of lives.

units.focus: Report on forecasts, warnings and damage
units.focusBn: পূর্বাভাস, সতর্কতা ও ক্ষয়ক্ষতির খবর জানানো

sessions.pattern: Subject + be (is / was / has been / will be) + past participle (+ by ...).
sessions.tipBn: কে কাজটি করেছে তার চেয়ে কাজটি বেশি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ হলে be + past participle দিয়ে কর্মবাচ্য গঠন হয়।

items.en: Weather data is collected from more than forty stations across the country every three hours.
More than two hundred thousand people were evacuated before the cyclone struck the coast.
A new early warning system has been installed along the Teesta River.
Most forecasts are now produced by computer models running on powerful supercomputers.
Thousands of acres of crops were damaged by salt water during the storm surge.
The final report will be presented to the government at a climate conference in Geneva.

sessions.tipBn: be-verb এর পরে not বসিয়ে কর্মবাচ্যের না-বোধক রূপ হয়, যেমন hasn't been repaired।

items.en: The damaged embankment still hasn't been repaired, even though the monsoon starts next month.
Many remote villages in the hill districts are not covered by the new radar network.
The fishermen were not informed about the storm until it was too late.
Deaths caused by extreme heat are often not recorded accurately in rural hospitals.
The outdoor concert won't be held in Dhaka unless the heatwave eases.
No schools were damaged in the storm, thanks to the newly built flood walls.

sessions.tipBn: Is, Was, Has বা Will শুরুতে বসে, তারপর subject ও past participle দিয়ে কর্মবাচ্যের প্রশ্ন হয়।

items.en: Was the warning broadcast in local languages as well as in Bangla?
Are weather balloons still launched twice a day from the station at Dhaka airport?
Has the flood damage been assessed in all the affected districts yet?
Will the schools be used as shelters if the cyclone gets closer?
Were the garment factories closed during the worst days of the heatwave?
Is the accuracy of every forecast checked against the weather that actually happened?

sessions.pattern: Could you tell me / Do you know / I wonder + wh- word or whether + passive clause
sessions.tipBn: ভদ্রভাবে জানতে Could you tell me বা I wonder দিয়ে শুরু হয়; ভেতরের অংশে subject আগে বসে, প্রশ্নের মতো উল্টো ক্রম হয় না।

items.en: Could you tell me how the daily forecast is prepared at the weather office?
Do you know whether the flood warning has been lifted in Sirajganj?
I wonder how many trees were planted in Dhaka after last year's heatwave.
Could you explain how cyclones in the Bay of Bengal are named?
May I ask when the new embankment along the river will be completed?
I would like to know whether the rainfall figures have been checked for errors.

words.bn: ভুল আছে কিনা যাচাই করা হয়েছে

sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে বিভিন্ন কালের কর্মবাচ্য (is collected, was destroyed, are being built) ব্যবহার হয়েছে।

items.title: How a forecast is made
items.en: Every morning, thousands of weather readings are collected from stations, ships and satellites. The data is sent to the weather office, where it is fed into computer models. The results are then checked by experienced forecasters. Finally, the forecast is shared with television channels, newspapers and mobile apps. Even so, it is updated several times a day because the weather can change quickly.

items.title: After the storm surge
items.en: When the cyclone made landfall, the island was struck by a storm surge nearly three meters high. Hundreds of homes were destroyed, and the only road to the mainland was washed away. Relief supplies were flown in by helicopter the next day. Months later, new houses are being built on raised platforms. The villagers have been promised a stronger embankment, but no date has been set for the work.

items.title: Working in the heat
items.en: Last April, outdoor work was restricted in several cities during the hottest hours of the day. Construction sites were closed from noon until three o'clock, and extra water points were set up for rickshaw pullers. In garment factories, more fans were installed and shifts were shortened. These measures were welcomed by workers, but it is still not known whether they will be enforced every summer.

units.focus: Reflect on what could have been different
units.focusBn: কী ভিন্ন হতে পারত তা নিয়ে ভাবা

sessions.pattern: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle. / If + had + past participle, would + verb (now).
sessions.tipBn: অতীতের কাল্পনিক শর্তে If + had + past participle এবং ফলাফলে would have + past participle বসে; ফলাফল বর্তমানের হলে would + verb বসে।

items.en: If the warning had come a day earlier, the farmers would have saved their harvest.
If the mangroves had been protected, the storm surge would have caused far less damage.
If Tom had listened to Nadia, he would have brought proper rain boots.
If the city had kept its canals open, Dhaka would drain much faster today.
If Nadia had become a doctor, she would be treating heatstroke patients right now.
The embankment would have held if it had been built with better materials.

sessions.pattern: If + hadn't + past participle, wouldn't have + past participle / wouldn't + verb.
sessions.tipBn: শর্ত বা ফলাফলের অংশে hadn't, wouldn't have বা wouldn't বসিয়ে না-বোধক বাক্য হয়।

items.en: If the forecast hadn't been so accurate, thousands of people wouldn't have left in time.
The rice wouldn't have withered if the rains hadn't come so late.
If Nadia hadn't studied the river, the village wouldn't be protected today.
Tom wouldn't have caught a cold if he hadn't walked home in the rain.
If people hadn't cut down the hill forests, the landslides wouldn't have been so deadly.
If we weren't so dependent on air conditioning, the power grid wouldn't have failed last week.

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + would (have) + subject + ... + if + had + past participle?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে would have + past participle বসে, আর অতীতের শর্তটি If + had দিয়ে আসে।

items.en: What would have happened if the cyclone had hit the coast at high tide?
How many lives would have been saved if the shelters had been closer?
Where would the families have gone if the school had stayed locked?
How would life in the coastal villages be different today if the embankments had been raised?
Which crops would the farmers have planted if they had known about the drought?
What would Nadia be doing now if she had stayed in London after her PhD?

sessions.pattern: 4–6 sentences with third and mixed conditionals.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে If + had + past participle দিয়ে অতীতের কাল্পনিক শর্ত, আর would have বা would দিয়ে তার সম্ভাব্য ফল বলা হয়েছে।

items.title: The warning that came late
items.en: Nadia often thinks about the flash flood in Sunamganj. If the rain gauges upstream had been connected to the warning system, farmers would have had two extra days. They would have harvested their rice early, and many families would not be in debt today. If the authorities had acted on her report, the story would have ended differently.

items.title: Tom's lucky escape
items.en: Last July, Tom missed his train from Sylhet by five minutes, and that train was later trapped by a landslide. If he had caught it, he would have spent two days stuck in the hills. If a local driver hadn't offered him a ride, he would have missed the conference in Dhaka. If he had checked the forecast, he would have left a day earlier and avoided all the stress.

items.title: A different Dhaka
items.en: Nadia sometimes imagines a different Dhaka. If planners had protected the wetlands fifty years ago, the city would not flood after every heavy shower. If more trees had been planted along the roads, summer afternoons would feel much cooler now. And if the canals hadn't been filled in, rickshaws wouldn't be wading through dirty water every monsoon. She believes it is not too late to learn from those mistakes.
